name: Rotoscoping. Supplemental design reference in the Animation Techniques category. The source collection does not name it as a direct style.
visualIdentity: Frame-by-frame tracing or reconstruction of actual filmed movement. Contours, fills, and simplification rules stay consistent across frames, preserving weight and proportions. Random edge changes are avoided. Generated movement or an ordinary filter does not qualify as rotoscoping.
suitableUses: Explicit suitable uses are unspecified for this style. Inferred from the listed combinations: music videos, documentary vignettes, and editorial films built from supplied footage. Biomechanics, sports, and dance analysis are also inferred, with overlays. These are inferences, not stated facts.
limitations: Requires a verified live-action reference. Without footage, the gap must be reported. Tracing must actually occur; Python or OpenCV assistance does not prove it. Simulated appearance is not evidence of photographed production. No renderer is listed. Listed alternatives are Blender Grease Pencil and Remotion.
palette: Reference-dependent example, not an intrinsic style palette. Background #F1EBDD, foreground #314249, and accent_1 #9D8A72 are three discrete colors, with gradients disabled. Foreground on background measures 8.807:1, meeting normal text targets. Accent on foreground measures 3.146:1, so it is decorative only. Approved task colors override these values, and assets must not be recolored.
motionAndInteraction: Motion follows the filmed source. No fixed engine or cadence is mandated, and stop-motion stepping is not imposed by the name alone. Held poses are preserved when used. Springs, bounce, and extra in-betweens are not added automatically. Motion references motion-012 (chaptered transitions) and motion-015 (narrative storytelling) are optional candidates only, screened for scene fit. Video runs on composition time, while scroll interaction is optional.
audio: The source sets no fixed audio rule for this style, so audio is unspecified. Choices should follow the topic, audience, and any explicit requirements. Options include narration, music, restrained sound accents, or silence. Final checks should confirm speech intelligibility, balance, absence of clipping, and picture synchronization.
assetRequirements: Requires filmed live-action footage as the movement reference. Inputs are prepared layers or numbered frames with alpha transparency, consistent dimensions, clear naming, and a layer manifest. Krita can draw frames and export numbered PNG sequences. Python or OpenCV is optional for extraction and alignment. Any audio must be authorized or task-provided.
combinations: Used alone, it suits realistic traced motion. Optional hybrid style-049 applies a two-ink riso fill using #314249 and #9D8A72 on #F1EBDD, with fixed grain and constant registration. No third ink is allowed. Optional hybrid style-109 adds thin overlays in #9D8A72 derived from traced positions. Overlays must not invent measurements or obscure the figure.
productionApproach: HyperFrames is the default pipeline, handling composition, timing, audio sync, validation, and export only. Remotion is a fallback, used only if HyperFrames is unavailable or has a verified limitation, and that reason must be recorded. Traced layers own visuals and motion. Verify decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames, sync, dimensions, duration, and loop seams. Separate drawing exposure rate from delivery frame rate.
